;Armed conflicts and attacks 
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**The [[United Nations]] remove [[Saudi Arabia]] from a blacklist of countries accused of "killing or maiming children, following a sustained significant decrease in air strikes". Saudi Arabia had threatened to cut funding to the UN. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-un/saudi-led-coalition-in-yemen-cut-from-u-n-blacklist-of-parties-killing-children-idUSKBN23M2R7?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**The [[Malian Armed Forces|armed forces]] say an [[ambush]] on a military convoy in central [[Mali]] has killed at least 24 troops and left others missing. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53058690 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/dozens-troops-dead-missing-northwest-mali-attack-200615142301025.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**The [[United States Department of Commerce|U.S. Department of Commerce]] announces it will relax the blacklist against [[Huawei]] to allow American companies to work with the Chinese telecom on setting [[5G]] network standards. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-china-huawei-tech-exclusive/u-s-companies-can-work-with-huawei-on-5g-other-standards-commerce-department-idUSKBN23M2DF?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A [[United States Air Force]] [[48th Fighter Wing]] [[McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle|F-15 Eagle]] based at [[RAF Lakenheath]], [[Great Britain|England]] crashes into the [[North Sea]], {{convert|74|mi|km}} off the [[East Riding of Yorkshire|East Yorkshire]] coast, killing the pilot. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/uk-england-suffolk-53051437 (BBC News)]
*At least three houses are damaged after an [[Indonesian Air Force]] [[British Aerospace Hawk 200|Hawk 209]] crashes into a residential area of [[Kampar Regency|Kampar]], [[Riau]]. There are no fatalities in the incident. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/15/three-houses-in-riau-damaged-by-crashing-indonesian-air-force-hawk-209-jet-fighter.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[United States House of Representatives|Rep.]] [[Tom Rice]] (R-SC) tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], becoming the 8th member of [[United States Congress|Congress]] to do so. [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/502768-house-gop-lawmaker-tests-positive-for-covid-19?amp (''The Hill'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***The [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) and [[UNICEF]] warn that 51,000 children could die in [[West Asia]] and [[North Africa]] due to the disruptive impact of the [[pandemic]] on healthcare systems. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/coronavirus-mena-who-unicef-warns-children-deaths (''Middle East Eye'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Killing of Rayshard Brooks]]
**The [[Fulton County, Georgia|Fulton County]] [[medical examiner]] declares Rayshard Brooks' death a [[homicide]]. Brooks was shot in the back by an [[Atlanta Police Department|Atlanta Police]] officer while fleeing from an attempted arrest for [[driving under the influence]] in which he stole an officer's taser and fired it at him on June 12. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53047282 (BBC News)]
*[[LGBTQ rights in the United States]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States]] delivers its decision in the case of ''[[Bostock v. Clayton County, Georgia]]'', ruling that the [[Civil Rights Act of 1964]] prohibits [[employment discrimination]] against individuals on the basis of their [[sexual orientation]] and [[gender identity]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-53055632 (BBC News)]
*Hundreds of [[National Police (France)|French police]] are brought in as reinforcements to the city of [[Dijon]], as over 150 [[Chechens]] from around France have gathered to avenge the alleged assault of a Chechen teenager by local [[drug dealer]]s. During the violence, several people are reported injured and one person suffered gunshot wounds. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53058981 (BBC News)] [https://www.jpost.com/international/france-sends-police-to-dijon-after-chechens-face-gangland-war-in-city-631606 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Maria Ressa]], CEO of [[Philippines|Philippine]] news site [[Rappler]], is found guilty of [[libel]] by a [[Manila]] [[Regional Trial Court|court]] over a 2012 story linking a businessman to various crimes. She faces up to six years in prison. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-media/philippine-court-finds-news-site-chief-maria-ressa-guilty-of-libel-idUSKBN23M03B?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Sudan]]'s public prosecutor announces the discovery of a [[mass grave]] containing the remains of students who were killed in 1998 when they tried to evade [[conscription]]. The [[prosecutor]] accused former ruler [[Omar al-Bashir]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudan-announces-discovery-of-mass-grave-of-students-killed-under-bashir-idUSKBN23M1OM?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A court in [[Russia]] sentences former [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] [[Paul Whelan (security director)|Paul Whelan]] to 16 years in prison for [[espionage]]. The [[List of ambassadors of the United States to Russia|U.S ambassador to Russia]] [[John J. Sullivan (diplomat)|John Sullivan]] condemns the sentencing as "a mockery of justice" in a statement to media after the verdict. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/15/world/paul-whelan-sentenced-russia-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Black Lives Matter]] activist [[Oluwatoyin Salau]] is found dead in [[Tallahassee, Florida]], US, after going missing on June 6. Shortly before her disappearance, Salau [[Twitter|tweeted]] that she had been [[sexually assault]]ed by a black man. Her death is currently being treated as a [[homicide]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/15/us/toyin-salau-black-lives-matter-found-dead-trnd/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Government of Nepal|Nepali Department of Immigration]] says that it will deport five foreign tourists (three Chinese, an American and an Australian) and ban them from entering [[Nepal]] for two years after they joined protests against the government's response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal|coronavirus outbreak]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/nepal-to-deport-foreign-tourists-for-joining-coronavirus-protest-12837948 (CNA)]
